title: Tema Oncology ETF (CANC) Rallies +13.6% Amid Key Oncology Advances
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
# Key Takeaways

* The Tema Oncology ETF surged approximately 13.6% over the past 30 days, driven by a wave of landmark oncology drug approvals and positive clinical data.
* Over the last quarter, CANC delivered a total return of roughly 12.2%, reflecting sustained momentum across the biotechnology and precision oncology sectors.
* The fund's largest holding, [Revolution Medicines](https://tickeron.com/ticker/RVMD/), saw its stock soar after the FDA approved daraxonrasib—the first-ever targeted therapy for pancreatic cancer—on July 8.
* Broader strength in holdings such as [Gilead Sciences](https://tickeron.com/ticker/GILD/), [Guardant Health](https://tickeron.com/ticker/GH/), and [Moderna](https://tickeron.com/ticker/MRNA/) amplified the rally, fueled by regulatory wins and growing investor enthusiasm for next-generation cancer treatments.
* The actively managed ETF, which concentrates on companies developing cancer therapeutics and diagnostics, benefited from a powerful sector-wide rotation into oncology and precision medicine names.

# Tema Oncology ETF (CANC) Overview and Portfolio Exposure

The Tema Oncology ETF (CANC) is an actively managed exchange-traded fund that invests in biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies shaping the future of cancer treatment and care. Launched in August 2023 and managed by Tema ETFs, the fund is overseen by portfolio manager David K. Song, MD, PhD, CFA, a Penn-trained physician with more than two decades of healthcare investing experience. CANC carries a net expense ratio of 0.75% and held approximately $197 million in assets under management (AUM) as of early July 2026.

The portfolio comprises roughly 58 holdings, with approximately 98% allocated to the healthcare sector. Top positions include [Revolution Medicines](https://tickeron.com/ticker/RVMD/) (6.0%), [Eli Lilly](https://tickeron.com/ticker/LLY/) (5.0%), [Cogent Biosciences](https://tickeron.com/ticker/COGT/) (5.0%), Novartis (3.9%), Roche Holding (3.8%), [Merck](https://tickeron.com/ticker/MRK/) (3.4%), [Legend Biotech](https://tickeron.com/ticker/LEGN/) (3.4%), [Immunome](https://tickeron.com/ticker/IMNM/) (3.3%), [Johnson & Johnson](https://tickeron.com/ticker/JNJ/) (3.3%), and [Bristol-Myers Squibb](https://tickeron.com/ticker/BMY/) (3.2%). Geographically, U.S.-listed companies represent roughly 75% of assets, with Switzerland, the United Kingdom, and other regions accounting for the remainder. This concentrated exposure to high-conviction oncology names makes CANC particularly responsive to clinical trial outcomes, regulatory decisions, and sector-wide sentiment shifts. From what I see, the structure aligns well with investors focused on precision medicine themes.

# Tema Oncology ETF (CANC) Price Performance: Last 30 Days vs. Quarter

Over the 30-day period ending July 10, 2026, CANC climbed approximately 13.6%, rising from a closing price of $36.48 on June 10 to an intraday level near $41.46. The advance was not linear; the ETF experienced a pronounced inflection point in late June that accelerated into early July as multiple portfolio holdings delivered transformative news. The rally was characterized by strong upward momentum rather than gradual grinding, with daily trading volumes expanding notably during the final week of the period.

Looking at the broader quarterly picture, CANC posted a total return of approximately 12.2% for the three months ending June 30, 2026, according to fund data. This performance reflects a sustained recovery and expansion from earlier 2026 levels, supported by a favorable macroeconomic backdrop for growth-oriented biotechnology equities and a series of positive clinical and regulatory catalysts across the oncology landscape. I’m watching this closely as a signal of broader sector rotation.

# What Drove CANC Price in the Last 30 Days

The primary catalyst behind CANC's sharp 30-day advance was the historic FDA approval of Revolution Medicines' daraxonrasib on July 8, 2026—the first targeted therapy ever approved for pancreatic cancer. The drug demonstrated a doubling of overall survival in second-line metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, with median overall survival reaching 13.2 months versus 6.7 months for chemotherapy. As CANC's largest holding at roughly 6% of net assets, [Revolution Medicines](https://tickeron.com/ticker/RVMD/) experienced a dramatic stock price surge that directly lifted the ETF's net asset value (NAV).

Several other major holdings contributed meaningfully to the rally. [Gilead Sciences](https://tickeron.com/ticker/GILD/) advanced after securing U.S. and European approvals for Trodelvy in first-line metastatic triple-negative breast cancer in late June, reinforcing its oncology franchise. [Guardant Health](https://tickeron.com/ticker/GH/) surged approximately 14% in a single session after the FDA cleared its Guardant360 CDx liquid biopsy test as a companion diagnostic for a new HER2-mutant lung cancer therapy, marking the platform's 27th companion diagnostic indication. [Moderna](https://tickeron.com/ticker/MRNA/) rallied roughly 40% over the month as the company unveiled an in-vivo CAR-T program and outlined an expanded oncology pipeline during its Science Day presentation. Additionally, Novartis received FDA approval for Scemblix as a first-line treatment for chronic myeloid leukemia—the first new frontline mechanism in that disease since 2001.

Collectively, these developments ignited a powerful sector-wide rotation into oncology and precision medicine equities. Investor sentiment was further bolstered by strong fund flows into healthcare ETFs and growing conviction that the oncology innovation cycle is accelerating. The concentrated, actively managed structure of CANC amplified the impact of these stock-specific catalysts relative to broader healthcare benchmarks. # What Drove CANC Performance Over the Last Quarter

The quarterly performance of approximately 12.2% was underpinned by a broader recovery in biotechnology equities that began in the spring of 2026. After a period of consolidation in April and May, the sector gained traction as clinical data readouts at major medical conferences—including the American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) annual meeting—reinforced the therapeutic and commercial potential of next-generation oncology platforms. Positive Phase 3 results from Revolution Medicines' daraxonrasib, presented at ASCO and published in the New England Journal of Medicine, set the stage for the subsequent approval and rally.

Macroeconomic conditions also provided a supportive backdrop. Stabilizing interest rate expectations and a risk-on environment favored growth-oriented sectors such as biotechnology. Institutional capital flows into actively managed thematic ETFs increased, with CANC's AUM growing substantially over the period. The fund's emphasis on companies targeting RAS-addicted cancers, antibody-drug conjugates, liquid biopsy diagnostics, and immuno-oncology positioned it at the intersection of several of the most dynamic subsectors within healthcare. This thematic alignment, combined with stock-specific execution from major holdings, drove the sustained quarterly advance.

# CANC ETF Outlook: What Investors Should Watch Next

Looking ahead, several factors are likely to influence CANC's trajectory. The commercial launch of daraxonrasib by [Revolution Medicines](https://tickeron.com/ticker/RVMD/) will be closely watched, as the company transitions from a clinical-stage biotech to a commercial oncology enterprise. Early prescription data, payer coverage decisions, and revenue ramp metrics will provide critical signals about the drug's market adoption and, by extension, the valuation of CANC's largest holding.

Beyond individual stock catalysts, the broader oncology regulatory calendar remains active. Additional FDA decisions, European Medicines Agency reviews, and clinical data presentations at major medical meetings could sustain or disrupt sector momentum. The ongoing congressional probe into pharmaceutical companies' China-based clinical trial partnerships introduces a layer of geopolitical risk, though deal flow between Western and Chinese biotech firms has continued largely uninterrupted. Macroeconomic variables—particularly interest rate policy and inflation trends—will also influence the risk appetite for growth-oriented biotechnology equities. While the recent rally reflects genuine therapeutic breakthroughs, the concentrated nature of CANC's portfolio means that setbacks affecting any major holding could produce outsized downside moves. Investors should monitor these dynamics while recognizing that the fund's active management provides a degree of adaptability in responding to changing market conditions.
